title: Sufficiency of Scripture
definition: The sufficiency of Scripture is the truth that God's Word contains all that He intends His people to have as the final authority for salvation, doctrine, correction, godliness, and faithful obedience.
summary: Scripture is enough to teach believers the truth of salvation, shape sound doctrine, and equip God's people for faithful living.
christFocus: The sufficiency of Scripture rests in the sufficiency of Christ, whom Scripture reveals as the complete Savior, Lord, Shepherd, and hope of His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The sufficiency of Scripture does not mean the Bible answers every curiosity or gives technical instruction on every subject. It means Scripture gives all God intends His people to have as the final rule for knowing Him, receiving salvation, forming doctrine, growing in godliness, and obeying His will.

God has not left His church dependent on hidden knowledge, human speculation, or spiritual novelty. His Word reveals the Gospel, exposes sin, declares grace, teaches holiness, corrects error, and equips the saints for every good work.

Study tools, teachers, commentaries, and dictionaries can serve the church well, but they must remain servants under Scripture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many believers chase extra words, special formulas, or spiritual shortcuts because they do not believe Scripture is enough. This doctrine protects people from manipulation and confusion.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Use helpful resources, but test everything by Scripture. When you need guidance, correction, comfort, or wisdom, begin with God's Word and let it shape your doctrine and obedience.
